chunks: `Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn `Abd al-Wahhab al-Sijzi in Naysabur said: Abu Nasr Mansur ibn `Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Isbahani reported to us that `Ali ibn `Abd Allah said: al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Harrani said; Yahya ibn `Abd Allah ibn al-Dahhak said, on the authority of al-Awza'i, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abu Kathir, that The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was asked: "Shall we not guard you?" He (peace be upon him) said: "The guardian of every man is his death."
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali (AS) mean when he said 'The guardian of every man is his death'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam Ali (AS) uses the metaphor of 'guarding' to illustrate the concept of *Ajal* (appointed term), shifting the focus from physical protection to the divine decree of mortality. This highlights the Shia theological emphasis on *Hikmah* (divine wisdom) and *Qadr* (predestination), where death is not merely an end but a divinely guarded transition that no human guard can alter. The statement underscores the believer's reliance on God's timing rather than worldly safeguards, reinforcing the spiritual reality that life and death are under exclusive divine control.
